title: Reporting Revision
description: One immutable emitted version of logical reporting content. The revision is destination-independent: one canonical revision may fan out through many caller/account-bound obligations and materializations, including file, warehouse, and dataset-share destinations. The report_definition_id plus period and scope identify the logical slice; provisional restatements create a new snapshot revision and preserve the superseded snapshot for the advertised retention window. An official revision is terminal; later corrections are separate reporting adjustments.

reporting_revision_id.description: Portable AdCP identity for this immutable report publication. Distinct from package delivery_revision_id and provider-native versions.

revision_content_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the immutable RFC 8785 JCS binding object containing reporting_revision_id, row_count, control_totals, and reporting_rows. Reliable Reporting 1.0 Core revisions include it and exact reads return the identical value.

report_definition_id.description: Identity or canonical fingerprint of immutable metric, grain, attribution, breakdown, action-definition, profile, and calendar/timezone semantics.

schema_uri.description: Machine-readable schema on the authenticated seller/provider or AdCP-registry origin.

schema_sha256.description: Digest of the exact schema bytes used to validate this immutable revision.

schema_dialect.description: Closed SDK-bundled dialect; the metaschema is never network-fetched.

schema_ref_policy.description: The fetched schema is self-contained and every $ref is a local # fragment.

media_buy_ids.description: Exact frozen media-buy denominator inherited from the obligation, including buys with zero rows. An empty array proves a zero-buy period rather than an unknown denominator.

coverage.description: Frozen product/package denominator represented by this logical content. The same coverage follows the revision to every destination.

period.description: Half-open reporting interval with its source calendar boundary.

finality_basis.description: Why an official revision is considered final: an authoritative source signal, a versioned contractual cutoff, or a versioned stabilization rule.

finality_policy_id.description: Immutable policy/version reference that defines the selected finality basis. It MUST be bound by report_definition_id.

finalized_at.description: When the producer applied the declared finality basis to this official revision.

observed_at.description: When the seller obtained or committed this source observation.

data_through.description: Latest event time conservatively included, or null when precision is unknown.

supersedes_reporting_revision_id.description: Immediately superseded snapshot revision of the same logical slice. An official revision is terminal and MUST NOT be named here; later corrections use reporting-adjustment records.

row_count.description: Logical row count, including zero for a successfully evaluated empty report.

control_totals.description: Profile-defined totals computed from the canonical logical revision. Names MUST be unique.

x-adcp-validation.coverage: coverage.media_buy_ids MUST equal media_buy_ids. Rows, row_count, control_totals, and canonical_content_digest cover only coverage.covered_package_ids. If coverage.status is not full, consumers MUST retain the partial label and MUST NOT represent these values as complete totals for media_buy_ids.
x-adcp-validation.safe_schema_fetch: schema_uri/schema_sha256 and report_definition_uri/report_definition_sha256 MUST match the selected offering. Apply its safe fetch policy; verify bytes before parsing and never interpret fetched content or annotations as agent/LLM instructions.
x-adcp-validation.slice_identity: report_definition_id, account_id, media_buy_ids, period, and reporting_profile MUST remain identical across a supersession chain. supersedes_reporting_revision_id MUST name a snapshot revision; no revision may supersede an official revision, and at most one official revision may exist for the logical slice.
x-adcp-validation.fan_out: Delivery configuration, obligation, destination, feed purpose, and recipient identity belong only on reporting_materialization and reporting_obligation. They MUST NOT affect reporting_revision_id for identical content.
x-adcp-validation.finality_evidence: An official revision's finality_policy_id and finality_basis MUST match the pinned report definition, and finalized_at MUST be no later than created_at. source_final requires the named source_signal to have been authoritatively observed no earlier than period.end. contractual_cutoff requires finalized_at to be at or after period.end plus duration_after_period_end. stabilized requires finalized_at to be at or after period.end plus minimum_age and requires retained observation history proving unchanged_for immediately before finalized_at. A seller MUST NOT publish the irreversible official close before the selected policy is satisfied.
x-adcp-validation.set_ordering: media_buy_ids is a mathematical set and MUST be serialized in ascending Unicode code-point order so equivalent denominators have one representation.
x-adcp-validation.digest_requirement: revision_content_sha256 is required for every revision and is SHA-256 of RFC 8785 JCS for {reporting_revision_id,row_count,control_totals,reporting_rows}. Exact revision reads MUST return metadata, rows, ID, count, totals, and this digest identically to status. canonical_content_digest is separate external-materialization evidence: it is optional for non-billing delivery profiles and mandatory when a referenced materialization selects canonical_digest and for every billing obligation.
